context: Flow map data visualization showing US domestic migration between 12 major cities, with directed arrows sized by volume and nodes colored/sized by net migration.
first_impression: The US map outline renders as a distorted horseshoe/crescent shape rather than a recognizable US silhouette, while all city nodes and flow arrows are crammed into a tiny cluster in the lower-center of the canvas.
what_works: The Tol palette choice (blue for net in-migration, red for net out-migration) is deliberate and semantically meaningful. The legend is clean and correctly positioned with a proper visual hierarchy between the title, subtitle, and legend text.
what_doesnt: The simplified GeoJSON outline combined with the Albers projection produces an unrecognizable horseshoe shape that dominates the canvas — the US is not legible as a map. All 12 city nodes and their flow arrows are compressed into roughly 200x100px in a 1200x800 canvas, making labels overlap badly (Chicago, Denver, Dallas, Atlanta, Philadelphia are a jumbled mass) and arrow directions indistinguishable.
